title: Eikö + owner + ole + partitive
summary: Begin with Eikö, place the owner next, keep ole after the owner, and end with the partitive noun.
prerequisiteSkills: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions
objectives: Arrange a question as eikö + owner + ole + negative noun form.
Recognise the pattern, then produce it with the supporting words shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Begin with Eikö, place the owner next, keep ole after the owner, and end with the partitive noun.
keyPoints: Eikö + owner + ole + singular partitive noun

sections.title: Regular noun forms in these examples
paragraphs: These forms name the thing after ei ole. The prompts show the noun form whenever forming it is outside this lesson’s target.
keyPoints: kissa (“cat”) → kissaa (“a cat”): regular singular partitive
koira (“dog”) → koiraa (“a dog”): regular singular partitive
tyyny (“pillow”) → tyynyä (“a pillow”): regular singular partitive
peli (“game”) → peliä (“a game”): regular singular partitive

steps: Begin with Eikö, the negative yes/no question word.
Put minulla next. minulla means “I as the owner”.
Put ole after the owner; it remains separate from Eikö.
End with the complete partitive autoa (“a car”): Eikö + owner + ole + thing.
Begin with Eikö, the negative yes/no question word.
Put sinulla next. sinulla means “you as the owner” for one person.
Put ole after the owner; it remains separate from Eikö.
End with the complete partitive palloa (“a ball”): Eikö + owner + ole + thing.
Begin with Eikö, the negative yes/no question word.
Put hänellä next. hänellä means “he as the owner” or “she as the owner”; this example uses “she”.
Put ole after the owner; it remains separate from Eikö.
End with the complete partitive kynää (“a pen”): Eikö + owner + ole + thing.
Begin with Eikö, the negative yes/no question word.
Put meillä next. meillä means “we as the owner”.
Put ole after the owner; it remains separate from Eikö.
End with the complete partitive koiraa (“a dog”): Eikö + owner + ole + thing.
Begin with Eikö, the negative yes/no question word.
Put teillä next. teillä means “you as the owner” for a group.
Put ole after the owner; it remains separate from Eikö.
End with the complete partitive kirjaa (“a book”): Eikö + owner + ole + thing.
Begin with Eikö, the negative yes/no question word.
Put heillä next. heillä means “they as the owner”.
Put ole after the owner; it remains separate from Eikö.
End with the complete partitive kissaa (“a cat”): Eikö + owner + ole + thing.
Begin with Eikö, the negative yes/no question word.
Put minulla next. minulla means “I as the owner”.
Put ole after the owner; it remains separate from Eikö.
End with the complete partitive peliä (“a game”): Eikö + owner + ole + thing.
Begin with Eikö, the negative yes/no question word.
Put teillä next. teillä means “you as the owner” for a group.
Put ole after the owner; it remains separate from Eikö.
End with the complete partitive tyynyä (“a pillow”): Eikö + owner + ole + thing.

commonMistakes: Keep the requested order Eikö + owner + ole + partitive noun; the owner goes between Eikö and ole.
Do not lose ole or the noun ending while arranging the question.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Build “Don’t they have a ball?” Put the owner immediately after the question word. Use heillä (“they as the owner”) and palloa (“a ball”).

sentenceExplanation.pattern: eikö + possessor + fixed ole + singular partitive noun

parts.formation: Ei + the question ending -kö = eikö. The front-vowel ending follows ei, independently of the noun.

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: he has the learned possession form heillä; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Negative possession keeps ole after eikö, with every owner.
pallo + -a = palloa. This is the singular partitive, the noun form used when possession is denied.
